core_aesthetic_takeaways: The batch teaches that university competition information visualization is an evidence system: a research proposition must be supported by maps, timelines, taxonomies, process diagrams, charts, and application proof.
A high-density board can still feel ordered when one dominant anchor owns the composition and secondary modules follow a named reading path.
The heritage boards use dark purple or black fields, luminous gold hierarchy, radial ritual wheels, mask taxonomies, historical timelines, and pattern references.
The Longjing boards use blue-green isometric process landscapes, numbered steps, plant/material analysis, clean white information areas, and system display pages.
The strongest transfer value is not the exact illustration style, but the strategy of converting cultural material into analyzable visual evidence.
prompt_structure_lessons: Start with project context: university discipline competition, cultural research, information visualization.
Name the board role: research overview board, technical process board, heritage taxonomy board, or application proof board.
Define one dominant anchor before listing supporting modules.
Describe every cultural symbol by its information role: source evidence, taxonomy, map, timeline, pattern, process, chart, or application proof.
For dense copy, require verified text or use readable placeholder blocks.

safe_exact_text_candidates: project title when supplied by the user
section labels such as project introduction, design description, chart display, result display, process, taxonomy, timeline, application display
large bilingual title blocks if source text is provided
requires_source_confirmation: zodiac deity names and mask attributes
award marks, competition seals, and all watermark text
text_accuracy_policy.training_rule: Use this batch for structure, palette, board strategy, data-module grammar, and application-proof layout. Never train watermark text, social-media overlays, or unverifiable microcopy as positive targets.

risk_controls.risk: turning academic infovis into a commercial poster
risk_controls.mitigation: Keep academic-discipline-competition as the primary context and require research title, concept, evidence modules, and application proof.
Caption every affected source with watermark_contamination and exclude watermark atoms from positive prompts.
Use source-confirmed text for real deliverables; otherwise render microcopy as clean placeholder blocks.
Require every decorative motif to map to taxonomy, timeline, pattern reference, process, or data category.
Use one dominant anchor, named module groups, margins, divider lines, and a top-to-bottom or radial reading path.

recommended_training_use.stage_1_curation: Use as metadata-ready references for academic competition infovis after rights review.
recommended_training_use.stage_2_caption_tuning: Train captions to separate heritage ritual boards, isometric process boards, and dark technical cultural boards.
recommended_training_use.stage_3_lora_training: Keep as an academic-discipline-competition subset before mixing with commercial brand, packaging, or product-photo references.
recommended_training_use.stage_4_prompt_runtime: Use for PromptPacketV2 memory retrieval when prompts mention university competition, information visualization, Culture China, non-heritage, craft process, maps, timelines, or application proof.
